title: Norm-controlled generators of submodules of finite free Tate modules
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. For $r,s\ge0$ put $D=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_rangle$, the restricted-series ring of [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. For $f=\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}c_
u T^
u\in D$ set $\|f\|_G=\sup_
u|c_
u|$, and for $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_s)\in D^s$ set $\|x\|=\max_{1\le j\le s}\|x_j\|_G$, with $\|0\|=0$ when $s=0$. For every $D$-submodule $L\subseteq D^s$ there are an integer $h\ge0$ and vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_h\in L$ such that $\|v_i\|=1$ for every $i$ and, for every $x\in L$, there exist $f_1,\ldots,f_h\in D$ satisfying $x=\sum_{i=1}^h f_iv_i$ and $\|f_i\|_G\le\|x\|$ for all $i$. The empty family is allowed for $L=0$; no finite-generation hypothesis is imposed on $L$.

source.place: Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22 (PDF pages 23–24, one-based); online primary PDF read, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
If $L=0$, take the empty family; this also handles $s=0$. Otherwise $s>0$. Put $E=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_sangle$ and define $\iota(x)=\sum_{j=1}^s x_jY_j$. Its coefficient at $(
u,e_j)$ is the coefficient of $T^
u$ in $x_j$, and all other coefficients vanish. Thus the restrictedness definition gives $\iota(x)\in E$, $\|\iota(x)\|_G=\|x\|$, and injectivity. For $0
e x$, select any nonzero coefficient of magnitude $a>0$. Only finitely many coefficients of $\iota(x)$ have magnitude at least $a$, so their maximum is the maximum of all coefficient magnitudes. In particular the Gauss norm is attained, and its maximizing exponents form a finite nonempty set.

source.place: Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22 (PDF pages 23–24); agent-supplied homogeneous encoding and bounded-division proof of the same conclusion; online primary PDF read, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Use graded lexicographic order on $\mathbf N^{r+s}$, and for a nonzero series $F$ let $\lambda(F)$ be the largest exponent among its coefficients of maximal magnitude. Let $A=\{\lambda(\iota(x)):0\ne x\in L\}$. Each element has the form $(\nu,e_j)$. Let $B$ be the set of coordinatewise minimal elements of $A$. Distinct elements of $B$ are incomparable, so the cited antichain statement with $d=r+s$ makes $B$ finite. Every $\alpha\in A$ dominates an element of $B$: among $\beta\in A$ with $\beta\le\alpha$, choose one with least sum of coordinates; any strictly smaller element of $A$ would have a smaller sum. Enumerate $B=\{\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_h\}$.

source.place: Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22 (PDF pages 23–24); agent-supplied homogeneous encoding and bounded-division proof of the same conclusion; online primary PDF read, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For each $\beta_i$ choose $w_i\in L\setminus\{0\}$ with $\lambda(\iota(w_i))=\beta_i$, and let $c_i\ne0$ be the coefficient at $\beta_i$. Set $v_i=c_i^{-1}w_i\in L$ and $b_i=\iota(v_i)$. Multiplicativity of the absolute value on $K$ gives $\|v_i\|=\|b_i\|_G=1$ coefficient by coefficient, since $|c_i|=\|w_i\|$. Scaling all coefficients by the same nonzero constant preserves their relative magnitudes, hence $\lambda(b_i)=\beta_i$. These choices depend only on $L$, not on the element to be represented.

source.place: Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22 (PDF pages 23–24); agent-supplied homogeneous encoding and bounded-division proof of the same conclusion; online primary PDF read, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $x\in L$. Apply bounded convergent division in the $r+s$ variables of $E$ to $F=\iota(x)$ and the finite list $b_1,\ldots,b_h$ of norm one. It gives $q_1,\ldots,q_h,R\in E$ with $F=\sum_iq_ib_i+R$, $\|q_i\|_G\le\|x\|$ and $\|R\|_G\le\|x\|$. For every exponent $\gamma$ with nonzero coefficient in $R$ and every $i$, one has $\beta_i\nleq\gamma$ coordinatewise. These are exactly the norm and support clauses in the cited statement; it does not require the list to be a Gröbner basis.

source.place: Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22 (PDF pages 23–24); agent-supplied homogeneous encoding and bounded-division proof of the same conclusion; online primary PDF read, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $q\in E$ write $q_0\in D$ for its coefficients at $Y$-exponent $0$, and for $R\in E$ let $P(R)\in D^s$ have $j$th entry given by its coefficients at $Y$-exponent $e_j$. Both are restricted: for every $\epsilon>0$ the retained coefficients of magnitude at least $\epsilon$ form a subset of the finite such set for the original series. Also $\|q_0\|_G\le\|q\|_G$. Since $b_i=\sum_j(v_i)_jY_j$, the coefficient at $(\nu,e_j)$ of $q_ib_i$ is $\sum_{\alpha+\delta=\nu}(q_i)_{\alpha,0}(v_i)_{j,\delta}$: nonnegative $Y$-exponents force the $Y$-exponent of $q_i$ to be zero. Thus extracting these coefficients in the division identity gives $x=\sum_if_iv_i+z$ with $f_i=(q_i)_0\in D$ and $z=P(R)\in L$. Moreover every nonzero coefficient of $\iota(z)$ is the identical coefficient of $R$, so its exponent is not above any $\beta_i$.

source.place: Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22 (PDF pages 23–24); agent-supplied homogeneous encoding and bounded-division proof of the same conclusion; online primary PDF read, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: If $z\ne0$, its leading exponent $\lambda(\iota(z))$ belongs to $A$ and hence dominates some $\beta_i$ by Step 2. Its coefficient is nonzero in $R$, contradicting the support clause from Step 4. Therefore $z=0$, and $x=\sum_if_iv_i$ with $\|f_i\|_G\le\|q_i\|_G\le\|x\|$. The norm-one property was proved in Step 3. For $x=0$ the coefficients can also be chosen all zero. No finite generation or closedness of $L$ was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-8b7b4d885 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all three cited nodes in full. The statement matches Bosch's Lectures (Apr 2008) §1.3 Corollary 10, pp. 21–22, read via pdftotext: any T_n-submodule of T_n^s, under the max of Gauss norms, has generators of norm 1, and every x is Σ f_i x_i with |f_i| ≤ |x|. The proof is agent-written and correct. Step 1 encodes x as Σ x_j Y_j in K<T,Y>; this is isometric, and the norm is attained. Step 2 takes the coordinatewise-minimal grlex leading exponents; Dickson (Mathlib leaf, antichain clause) makes them finite, and every exponent dominates one of them by a least-coordinate-sum argument. Step 3 normalises by the leading coefficient; |c_i| = ‖w_i‖ and λ is unchanged. Step 4 applies lem-trf-tate-convergent-division in r+s variables with norm-1 b_i; its L(·) is the same grlex function as λ, and the norm and support clauses are quoted correctly. I checked that the division node is true by splitting each b_i into a unit-leading polynomial plus a part of norm ≤ ρ < 1 and iterating; this also works for dense value groups. Step 5: the Y-degree-1 coefficients of q_i b_i only involve the Y-exponent-0 slice of q_i, so x = Σ (q_i)_0 v_i + z with z in L. Step 6: z ≠ 0 would contradict the support exclusion. Checked the cases L=0, s=0, r=0 (a line (1,π)), s=1, L=D^s, and dense value groups. proof_deps equal the union of uses. There is no cycle (the division node has no proof_deps), the cited lemmas are in the item's own unit sk-i-curve-zero, there are no new nodes, and no duplicate exists in the DAG (lem-trf-tate-ideal-best-approximation is a different statement). Both citers use exactly the two clauses as stated. No SGA is cited. The source PDF is not in literature/ and is recorded as WANTED. No changes.
